root_cause.text: In `net/rxrpc/rxgk.c`, `rxgk_verify_response()` validated `rhdr.token_len` only after applying `xdr_round_up()`, so a crafted large `token_len` could overflow during rounding and bypass the packet-length check.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (xdr_round_up(token_len) + sizeof(__be32) > len)` to also reject `if (token_len > len || xdr_round_up(token_len) + sizeof(__be32) > len)`, and the commit message explicitly says the bug was “integer overflow due to rounding up token_len before checking it, thereby allowing the length check to be bypassed.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Tighten response length validation to reject packets whose token length exceeds the available data.
intent_record.what: The length check in rxgk_verify_response() was expanded from a single condition, `xdr_round_up(token_len) + sizeof(__be32) > len`, to two conditions: `token_len > len || xdr_round_up(token_len) + sizeof(__be32) > len`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now rejects responses where the token length itself exceeds the remaining packet length, in addition to the existing rounded-up XDR size check. This prevents invalid or malformed packets with an oversized token length from passing the validation and reaching later parsing logic.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly matches the root cause by tightening response length validation around token_len, which is the check that was previously performed too late after xdr_round_up() and could be bypassed via overflow.

candidates.rationale: This is the pre-fix point where the untrusted token length is read and later rounded up before validation; the vulnerability stems from validating after xdr_round_up() rather than rejecting oversized token_len values up front.

vuln_statements.explanation: This line reads the untrusted token length from the response header. The root cause is that the subsequent validation happened only after xdr_round_up(), allowing a crafted large token_len to overflow during rounding before the packet-length check.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable logic is present in `rxgk_verify_response()`. The code does `token_len = ntohl(rhdr.token_len);` and then immediately applies rounding in the length check: `if (xdr_round_up(token_len) + sizeof(__be32) > len) goto short_packet;`. This matches the root cause: validation happens only after `xdr_round_up()`, so a crafted large `token_len` could overflow during rounding before the packet-length check. The function does not contain any pre-rounding bounds check or overflow-safe validation, so the fix is not present here.
